10870-# Read-only rendering of tailscale servers already lives in cmd_server_instances.

10872-# are safe to flip after creation.
10873-#
10874-# Forkop stores a tailscale node as `config server` with protocol=tailscale, NOT
10875-# as a routing section, so none of the section helpers apply here. Of the six
10876-# tailscale_* options Forkop knows, only tailscale_auth_key has no default
10877-# (validateRequired in luci-app-forkop server.js); control_url, hostname and
10878-# advertise_exit_node are defaulted by server_default_set_option. We therefore
10879-# ask for the minimum and let Forkop fill the rest.
10880-#
10881-# control_url is asked for anyway because the default points at Tailscale's
10882-# cloud: on a self-hosted control plane (Headscale, ionscale, …) leaving the
10883-# default silently registers the node with the wrong network.
10884-

10886-# cross-talk when several admins use the bot. Format (v2): control URL on line 1,
10887-# requested node hostname on line 2 (empty while that prompt is pending), epoch on
10888-# line 3. The auth key is NEVER stored here. Legacy v1 files (URL + epoch) are
10889-# accepted so an in-flight wizard from hotfix11/12 can recover safely.

1149:# singbox_supports_tailscale: returns 0 if the running sing-box can serve a
1150-# tailscale endpoint.
1151-#
1152-# Mirrors Forkop's sing_box_supports_tailscale() (singbox/runtime.uc): an
1153-# "extended" build always qualifies, otherwise the build must carry the
1154-# with_tailscale tag. This MUST be checked before writing a tailscale server
1155-# section — Forkop's validator rejects the WHOLE config when a tailscale
1156-# section exists on a build without the tag, so a blind write does not just
1157-# fail to start the node, it takes routing down with it.
1158-#
1159-# Capability probing MUST NOT execute sing-box. A second Go process just for
1160-# `sing-box version` can exhaust the last tens of MiB on 256 MB routers and stall
1161-# the already-running dataplane. Prefer the shared provider helper; standalone
1162-# installs fall back to package/variant markers and a streaming binary tag scan.

1172-        opkg status sing-box-tiny 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: .* installed$' && return 1
1173-        opkg status sing-box-extended 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: .* installed$' && return 0
1174-    fi
1175-    if command -v apk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1176-        apk info -e sing-box-tiny >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 1
1177-        apk info -e sing-box-extended >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
1178-    fi
1179-    if [ -r /etc/forkop/sing-box-variant ]; then
1180-        grep -qiE 'extended|with_tailscale|tailscale' /etc/forkop/sing-box-variant 2>/dev/null && return 0
1181-        grep -qi 'tiny' /etc/forkop/sing-box-variant 2>/dev/null && return 1
1182-    fi
1183-

17021-# Kill any orphaned watchdog processes from a previous instance that survived

17023-# hold the lock so it won't be blocked — only the main loop holds it.
17024-BOT_LOCK_FILE="${BOT_DIR}/bot.lock"
17025-BOT_PID_FILE="${BOT_DIR}/bot.pid"
17026-# NOTE: stopping previous instances is the init.d script's job (it kills the
17027-# main + forked children by cmdline). This process does NOT kill anything on
17028-# startup — that risked killing a legitimate running instance and masking
17029-# init.d problems. Single-instance is enforced purely by the lock-guard below
17030-# ("refuse to start if a live instance already holds the lock"). We only record
17031-# our PID here for the cleanup trap and external tooling.
17032-printf '%s' "$$" > "$BOT_PID_FILE"

17034-# Clean up orphaned temp files from a previous run that was killed mid-cycle
17035-# (SIGKILL bypasses trap — these files are never rm'd by the dying process).
17036-# Only remove files older than 60s to avoid racing with a concurrent startup.
17037-find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name 'podkop_req.*' -o -name 'podkop_updates.*' \

17047-logger -t podkop-bot "=== Podkop Bot v${BOT_VERSION} Starting ==="
17048-
17049-# ── Single-instance guard ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
17050-# The init.d/procd script supervises only the main PID, but this bot forks a
17051-# health daemon + startup-notify child that keep polling getUpdates. A failed
17052-# stop or a respawn can leave the old children alive while a new main starts,
17053-# producing TWO concurrent getUpdates pollers on one token → Telegram 409
17054-# Conflict, flapping routes, and no startup card. Guard against it: refuse to
17055-# start if a live instance is already running.
17056-mkdir -p "$BOT_DIR" 2>/dev/null
17057-_LOCK_PID_FILE="${BOT_DIR}/podkop_bot.pid"

17059-    _old_pid=$(cat "$_LOCK_PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
17060-    # Is that PID still a live podkop_bot process? (not just any reused PID)
17061-    if [ -n "$_old_pid" ] && [ -d "/proc/$_old_pid" ] && \
17062-       grep -qa 'podkop_bot' "/proc/$_old_pid/cmdline" 2>/dev/null; then
17063-        logger -t podkop-bot "FATAL: another podkop_bot instance is already running (PID ${_old_pid}). Refusing to start a second poller (would cause Telegram 409 Conflict). If this is wrong, remove ${_LOCK_PID_FILE} and restart."
17064-        exit 1
17065-    fi
17066-    # stale pidfile (process gone) — clean it up and continue
17067-    rm -f "$_LOCK_PID_FILE"
